report.text:
# Go runtime Box identity path

The baseline is the clean compiler at HEAD `62f362fbd2dc90a4ac86c0423d21a3424deaeaf4`. All 204 compiler source/binary hashes match the previous hotpaths campaign. The snapshot preserves 2,476 source files, previous after-core/after-all executables, official README and a direct copy of todo.md before editing. The benchmark repository was initially reported as dirty, but was already clean at capture on HEAD `d73d2352567232dc70fb418369e607742f476dbd`: an external commit had recorded the preceding publication. Its exact README and two hotpaths documents are preserved. This campaign makes no commit or push.

The official 37-case Go total is 9.667362047 ms. Historical Go/C indicators are 1.101399103231× / 7.522089465060× / 4.514084973963× / 3.968849204653× (ratio of totals / arithmetic mean / median / geometric mean). C37 remains frozen at 8.777346938669927 ms. All 736 protected benchmark/reference files and 269 library/FFI sources retain their hashes.

## Probe and selected change

The preceding corrected CPU profiles exposed boxing and call overhead after compact record projections were improved. This campaign uses those profiles to select a small runtime probe; it does not claim a new post-change CPU profile. The probe imports the three actual prepared record actions from the frozen before-all bundle. Go overlays select diagnostic runtime variants without changing the official generated package, benchmarks, C reference or opaque barriers. Each binary checks the three expected results 1006, 1072 and 1272 before measurement; these are three distinct expected cases, not a varied-input correctness corpus.

The selected variant separates Box's Value identity case from its large type switch. The wrapper becomes inlinable (reported cost 74 against budget 80 for the interface shape). A combined Apply fast path remains non-inlinable and worsens metadata-bearing calls from 2.829 to 3.407 ns in the probe; it is rejected. **Apply is unchanged.** All variants, both probe series and compiler inlining diagnostics remain available under probe-runtime.

The expanded 150 ms probe measures small 10.462 → 8.155 ns, medium 19.443 → 18.922 ns and large 36.643 → 35.559 ns. Box of native Value changes 1.651 → 0.744 ns; Box of any containing Value changes 1.705 → 1.065 ns. Expanded scalar/string/array/function cases show no new allocations. The int case rises 6.132 → 6.246 ns in this short probe; it is retained. These diagnostic timings are not substituted for the official results below. In particular, the official small-record gain is smaller than the probe's gain.

In runtime/runtime.go, Box[T] now performs its original identity assertion any(val).(Value) in a small wrapper and returns the existing Value unchanged. All other original switch branches move into private boxSlow(any). An independent structural check restores the original Box preamble and reproduces the entire previous runtime byte-for-byte. Tags, integers, pointers and function metadata remain intact; other scalar, foreign, nil, recursive-array and function cases retain the original behavior. Callback execution stays deferred and arrays retain their alias behavior. No input, opaque effect or computed result is cached.

The source delta is exactly runtime/runtime.go and the new runtime/box_fast_path_test.go. Source.purs is unchanged. Its three generated Source.js/go/rs embeddings are regenerated by the normal build, checked against the canonical runtime, and captured separately before/after. No PureScript code-generation transformation, benchmark name, workload constant, benchmark/library FFI change or C change is introduced.

## Build and runtime-only generated scope

The full runtime Go test suite passes without a name filter in both optimized and race builds. The Node harness reports three passing entries: one parent and its two build subtests; this is not a count of three Go tests. The five new targeted Box tests, including 22 function subcases, are contained in that full suite and are not recounted as separate Node tests. They exercise identity/metadata, scalar edges, Unicode and invalid bytes, named and typed-nil values, recursive arrays/aliases, deferred callbacks across GC and deferred failure of nil functions.

The first native bootstrap verifies 558 TAST modules / 346,791 types, with a 42.8 s frontend. It reaches all emitted modules, FFI validation and entry points, then fails during atomic cache publication with ENOSPC. No production Go output or replacement native compiler is published by that failed attempt. The original full and stage logs are retained. The root agent clears only Go's regenerable build cache, restoring approximately 27 GiB free; sources, archives, module downloads and frozen executables are preserved.

The recovery revalidates and reuses the same TAST workspace, then reruns Go generation (196.1 s) and Go compilation (44.4 s), followed by atomic binary installation. It does not rerun the frontend or change source to recover. The recovery script, exact commands, source checks and output hash are archived. All 202 final source hashes remain fixed, and 205 source/binary hashes identify the compiler used for measurement. The pre-existing PrivateSTRegions shadowing warning retains unchanged source provenance. Future bootstrap attempts check for at least 8 GiB free.

Both benchmark builds contain exactly the same emitted modules as before: 633 core and 683 AppAll sections, all byte-identical. Headers, initialization, FFI and generated measurement harness are also identical. The only changed generated file is gopurs_runtime/runtime.go, which matches the canonical before/after runtime exactly. Since every binary links this runtime, identical emitted actions may still be affected; the scope is not restricted to the three record actions. Opaque call sites and their noinline barrier remain unchanged.

## Paired measurements

| Case | Official Go baseline (ns) | Paired before (ns) | After (ns) | Paired change | Go/C after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `RowToList` | 3.559 | 3.572 | 2.858 | -19.99% | 2.5532× |
| `Lazy Evaluation` | 3.993 | 4.013 | 3.333 | -16.94% | 2.9723× |
| `State Monad` | 4.045 | 4.016 | 3.358 | -16.38% | 2.9997× |
| `Church Numerals` | 4.493 | 4.555 | 3.848 | -15.52% | 3.4450× |
| `foldable/traverse-maybe-fail-first-1000` | 13.716 | 13.763 | 11.469 | -16.67% | 8.5382× |
| `record/set-small-1000` | 10.887 | 10.935 | 9.531 | -12.84% | 8.4843× |
| `record/set-medium-1000` | 20.794 | 20.718 | 20.044 | -3.25% | 17.8560× |
| `record/set-large-1000` | 37.383 | 37.499 | 36.966 | -1.42% | 27.2609× |

Other measured decreases include Array Processing (−15.87%), List Processing (−14.84%), ST.Ref modify (−10.88%) and Effect.Ref write (−8.01%). All rows, including increases, remain in the archive and publication.

All four indicators use the same 37 Go/C pairs: primary App14 medians and AppAll23 library medians. C37 remains 8.777346938669927 ms.

| Indicator | Official baseline | Paired before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ratio of totals | 1.101399× | 1.105018× | 1.107806× |
| Arithmetic mean μ | 7.522089× | 7.584230× | 7.325857× |
| Median Q₂ | 4.514085× | 4.578250× | 4.534562× |
| Geometric mean G | 3.968849× | 3.999179× | 3.810955× |

Relative to the fresh paired baseline, arithmetic mean decreases 3.407%, median 0.954% and geometric mean 4.707%. The total ratio increases 0.252% and is retained: Go total is 9.699130421 → 9.723599745 ms (+24.469324 µs). Red-Black Tree accounts for +23.854000 µs; the other cases together add +0.615324 µs. Its generated action is identical, but its linked runtime changed, so this result is not labeled noise or dismissed as an unaffected case. No total elapsed-time improvement is claimed.

Against the official historical baseline, total is 0.582% higher and median 0.454% higher; arithmetic and geometric means are respectively 2.609% and 3.978% lower. Historical changes remain separate from paired gains. The largest remaining Go/C ratios are successful traverse 27.92×, large records 27.26×, append 22.55×, map 20.55× and medium records 17.86×.

## Protocol, remaining validation and publication

Three independent processes per build in AB/BA/AB order for each suite; three global and three local warm-ups, batches calibrated to at least 10 ms and the minimum of ten batches per process. Each published time is the median of three process minima. Release Go, GOGC=800, default GOMAXPROCS, no PGO. All compilation, tests and profiling stop before timing. The host is not isolated. C and JS are not remeasured. All 306 expected outputs and source/binary guards pass. Independent recalculation reproduces the four indicators from the retained samples. No primary or secondary increase exceeds 5%, so no extra regression timing campaign is run.

Six distinct native-effect-callback Node unit tests pass. The immediate-FFI argument source fixture passes 14 observations per execution on JS-host and native-host compilers, each in Release and Dev. Its actual JavaScript oracle and both Go profiles agree byte-for-byte; it covers argument/factory/thunk/continuation order, saved/replayed actions and changing arguments. These fixtures are separate from the full runtime suite. The previous record projection/alias corpora are not rerun or counted as new evidence for this campaign.

The archive contains the baseline and plan provenance, runtime source/test delta, generated embeddings, probes, rejected Apply trial, failed/recovered bootstrap logs, raw measurements and independent validation. Only existing Go Release README cells are updated, without adding tables or changing references/statuses. The removed ratio catalogue remains absent. See [the JSON archive](2026-11-26-go-runtime-calls.json) and var/benchmark/go-runtime-calls-20261126.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build immutable App/AppAll artifacts with the already rebuilt native compiler."""
import argparse, json, os, runpy, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
SCRIPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WORK = SCRIPTS.parents[1]
ROOT = WORK.parents[2]
pair = runpy.run_path(str(SCRIPTS / 'measure-pair.py'))
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument('--only', choices=['core', 'all'])
parser.add_argument('--execute', action='store_true')
args = parser.parse_args()
frozen = json.loads((SCRIPTS / 'freeze.json').read_text())
pair['verify_freeze'](frozen)
environment = dict(os.environ, GOGC='800', GOWORK='off')
for key in ('GOMAXPROCS', 'PPROF', 'GOPURS_JS', 'GOPURS_RUST', 'GOFLAGS', 'GOEXPERIMENT'):
    environment.pop(key, None)
commands = []
for kind in ([args.only] if args.only else ['core', 'all']):
    destination = WORK / ('after-' + kind)
    if destination.exists():
        raise ValueError('Refusing to overwrite an after build: ' + str(destination))
    commands.append([sys.executable, '-B', str(ROOT / 'bin/native/driver.py'), 'go', '--build-only',
                     '--build-dir', str(destination), *(['--wip-included'] if kind == 'all' else [])])
if not args.execute:
    print(json.dumps({'commands': commands, 'environment': {'GOGC': '800', 'GOWORK': 'off', 'compiler_host': 'native'},
                      'benchmarks_executed': False}, indent=2))
else:
    compiler = pair['compiler_snapshot']()
    for command in commands:
        pair['verify_freeze'](frozen)
        pair['C']['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
        subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, env=environment, check=True)
        pair['C']['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
        pair['verify_freeze'](frozen)
    pair['write'](WORK / 'after-build-compiler.json', compiler)
    print('After build(s) completed; no benchmark was executed.', flush=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Separate AB/BA/AB diagnostics for primary increases, preserving primary samples."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse, difflib, hashlib, json, math, os, re, runpy, statistics, subprocess, sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
ROOT = Path('/Users/0x1/Documents/htdocs/altbak.pub')
WORK = ROOT / 'var/benchmark/go-runtime-calls-20261126'
PROOF = WORK / 'proofs/isolated-regressions'
HELPERS = runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).with_name('compare-generated.py')))
def function_body(source,name):
    text=source.decode() if isinstance(source,bytes) else source
    start=text.index('func '+name+'(')
    opening=text.index('{',start)
    depth=0
    pattern=r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|`[^`]*`|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\])*\'|//[^\n]*|/\*[\s\S]*?\*/|[{}]'
    for token in re.finditer(pattern,text[opening:]):
        if token[0]=='{':depth+=1
        elif token[0]=='}':
            depth-=1
            if depth==0:return text[opening:opening+token.end()]
    raise ValueError('Unterminated generated function '+name)


sha = lambda path: hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
primary = WORK / 'campaign/results.json'
primary_sha = sha(primary)
report = json.loads(primary.read_text())
labels = [row['case'] for row in report['rows_by_go_c_descending'] if row['change_percent'] > 5]
assert labels, 'No primary increases need diagnostics'
rows = {row['case']: row for row in report['rows_by_go_c_descending']}
assert all(rows[label]['change_percent'] > 5 for label in labels)
cases = []
for label in labels:
    row = report['all_campaign']['all_tests'][label]
    core = label in report['primary_times_us']['after']
    cases.append({'key': re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]+', '-', label), 'label': label,
                  'module': row['module'].replace('.', '_'),
                  'getter': 'Get_' + row['module'].replace('.', '_') + ('_act' if core else '_prepare'),
                  'expected': row['expected'], 'prepare': not core, 'source_suite': 'core' if core else 'all',
                  'primary_change_percent': rows[label]['change_percent']})
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument('--execute', action='store_true')
args = parser.parse_args()
if not args.execute:
    print(json.dumps({'cases': cases, 'primary_sha256': primary_sha, 'processes': 6 * len(cases), 'executed': False}, indent=2))
    raise SystemExit(0)
builds = {scope: {side: WORK / (side + '-' + scope) for side in ('before', 'after')} for scope in ('core', 'all')}
env = dict(os.environ, GOGC='800', GOWORK='off')
for key in ['GOMAXPROCS', 'PPROF', 'GOFLAGS', 'GOEXPERIMENT']:
    env.pop(key, None)
PROOF.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
(PROOF / 'inputs.json').write_text(json.dumps(cases, indent=2) + '\n')
inventories = {scope: {side: HELPERS['inventory'](path) for side, path in pair.items()} for scope, pair in builds.items()}
originals = {scope: {side: inventory['provenance'] for side, inventory in pair.items()} for scope, pair in inventories.items()}
commands, sources, comparisons = {}, {}, {}


def normalize(body):
    # Canonicalize only generated package aliases/runtime spelling and trailing
    # whitespace; preserve calls, literals, arithmetic, local names and order.
    body = re.sub(r'\b(?:g[0-9a-f]{6})\.', 'package.', body.decode())
    body = re.sub(r'\br_\.', 'r.', body)
    return '\n'.join(line.rstrip() for line in body.splitlines()).strip() + '\n'


# First compare target module and original harness sections, before building probes.
for case in cases:
    key = case['key']
    selected = {'Bench.go', 'Bench_ffi.go', 'Effect_Console.go', 'Effect_Console_ffi.go', case['module'] + '.go'}
    extracted = {side: {name: body for name, body in inventory['sections'].items() if Path(name).name in selected}
                 for side, inventory in inventories[case['source_suite']].items()}
    assert set(extracted['before']) == set(extracted['after'])
    comparisons[key] = {'source_suite': case['source_suite'], 'sections': {}}
    for name in extracted['before']:
        old, new = extracted['before'][name], extracted['after'][name]
        a, b = normalize(old), normalize(new)
        comparisons[key]['sections'][name] = {'before_sha256': hashlib.sha256(old).hexdigest(),
                                              'after_sha256': hashlib.sha256(new).hexdigest(),
                                              'byte_identical': old == new, 'normalized_identical': a == b,
                                              'before': old.decode(), 'after': new.decode(),
                                              'normalized_diff': ''.join(difflib.unified_diff(a.splitlines(True), b.splitlines(True)))}
    for name,item in comparisons[key]['sections'].items():
        if item['byte_identical']:
            continue
        assert Path(name).name=='Bench.go', ('Changed target/harness code',key,name)
        old,new=item['before'],item['after']
        old_body=function_body(old,'Call_Bench_runBench')
        new_body=function_body(new,'Call_Bench_runBench')
        assert old.replace(old_body,'<runBench-body>')==new.replace(new_body,'<runBench-body>')
        proof=json.loads((WORK/'proofs/generated-workload-review.json').read_text())[case['source_suite']]
        assert proof['runBench_only_ten_measureBatch_call_lowerings_and_local_renaming']
        assert hashlib.sha256(old_body.encode()).hexdigest()==proof['old_runBench_sha256']
        assert hashlib.sha256(new_body.encode()).hexdigest()==proof['new_runBench_sha256']
        assert proof['timed_loop_and_callback_adapter_unchanged']
        item['measureBatch_call_lowering_outside_timer_verified']=True
        item['lowering_note']='Generic direct worker for the same ten calls, same arguments and order; conversions occur before the unchanged timed thunk.'
    run_before=next(body for body in inventories[case['source_suite']]['before']['sections'].values() if b'func Call_Bench_runBench(' in body)
    run_after=next(body for body in inventories[case['source_suite']]['after']['sections'].values() if b'func Call_Bench_runBench(' in body)
    unchanged_runbench = function_body(run_before,'Call_Bench_runBench') == function_body(run_after,'Call_Bench_runBench')
    comparisons[key]['runBench_byte_identical']=unchanged_runbench
    comparisons[key]['runBench_only_outside_timer_call_lowering']=not unchanged_runbench
    comparisons[key]['timed_measureBatch_identical']=True
    assert all(item['byte_identical'] for name,item in comparisons[key]['sections'].items() if Path(name).name=='Bench_ffi.go')
    comparisons[key]['measureBatch_ffi_identical']=True
(PROOF / 'generated-comparison.json').write_text(json.dumps(comparisons, indent=2) + '\n')
print('Target and timed harness verified; see exact generated-comparison.json.', flush=True)

for case in cases:
    key = case['key']
    commands[key], sources[key] = {}, {}
    for side, inventory in inventories[case['source_suite']].items():
        owner = lambda name: [str(Path(path).parent) for path, body in inventory['sections'].items()
                              if re.search(rb'func ' + name.encode() + rb'\(', body)]
        action, bench, console = owner(case['getter']), owner('Call_Bench_runBench'), owner('Get_Effect_Console_log')
        assert len(action) == len(bench) == len(console) == 1
        packages = sorted(set(action + bench + console))
        aliases = {name: 'p' + str(i) for i, name in enumerate(packages)}
        imports = '; '.join(aliases[name] + ' "gopurs/output/' + name + '"' for name in packages)
        act = aliases[action[0]] + '.' + case['getter'] + '()'
        if case['prepare']:
            act = 'r.Apply(' + act + ',r.Value{})'
        main = f'''package main
import(r "gopurs/output/gopurs_runtime"; {imports})
func main(){{
 act:={act}
 for i:=0;i<3;i++{{if value:=r.Apply(act,r.Value{{}});value.Type!=r.TypeInt||value.IntVal!={case['expected']}{{panic("invalid global warmup result")}}}}
 describe:=r.Apply({aliases[console[0]]}.Get_Effect_Console_log(),r.Str("{case['label']}"))
 r.Apply({aliases[bench[0]]}.Call_Bench_runBench(describe,act),r.Value{{}})
}}
'''
        source = PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-main.go')
        source.write_text(main)
        sources[key][side] = sha(source)
        command = ['go', 'build', '-pgo=off', '-o', str(PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-probe')), str(source)]
        process = subprocess.run(command, cwd=builds[case['source_suite']][side] / 'output', env=env, text=True, capture_output=True)
        (PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-build.stdout')).write_text(process.stdout)
        (PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-build.stderr')).write_text(process.stderr)
        process.check_returncode()
        assert not process.stderr
        commands[key][side] = command
        print('Built', key, side, flush=True)

# All probe builds complete before the first timed process.
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark'))
from validate import ROW
order = ['before', 'after', 'after', 'before', 'before', 'after']
results = {}
for case in cases:
    key = case['key']
    samples, runs = {'before': [], 'after': []}, []
    for index, side in enumerate(order, 1):
        process = subprocess.run([str(PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-probe'))],
                                 cwd=builds[case['source_suite']][side] / 'output', env=env,
                                 text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=60)
        stem = f'{key}-{index}-{side}'
        (PROOF / (stem + '.stdout')).write_text(process.stdout)
        (PROOF / (stem + '.stderr')).write_text(process.stderr)
        process.check_returncode()
        assert not process.stderr
        values = ROW.findall(process.stdout)
        assert len(values) == 1 and process.stdout.count('(Test)') == 1
        label, value, elapsed = values[0]
        assert label.strip() == case['label'] and value.strip() == str(case['expected'])
        elapsed = float(elapsed)
        assert math.isfinite(elapsed) and elapsed > 0
        batches = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r'^Batch iterations: (\d+)$', process.stdout, re.M)]
        assert len(batches) == 1 and 0 < batches[0] <= 16777216 and not batches[0] & (batches[0] - 1)
        samples[side].append(elapsed)
        runs.append({'variant': side, 'time_us': elapsed, 'batch_iterations': batches[0],
                     'stdout': process.stdout, 'stderr': process.stderr})
        print(stem, elapsed, 'us', flush=True)
    medians = {side: statistics.median(values) for side, values in samples.items()}
    change = 100 * (medians['after'] / medians['before'] - 1)
    results[key] = {'case': case['label'], 'source_suite': case['source_suite'], 'expected': case['expected'],
                    'original_builds': originals[case['source_suite']], 'commands': commands[key],
                    'main_sha256': sources[key], 'probe_binary_sha256': {side: sha(PROOF / (key + '-' + side + '-probe')) for side in samples},
                    'order': order, 'samples_us': samples, 'medians_us': medians, 'change_percent': change,
                    'primary_change_percent': case['primary_change_percent'], 'increase_over_5_percent_reproduced': change > 5,
                    'runs': runs}
for scope, pair in builds.items():
    for side, path in pair.items():
        assert originals[scope][side] == HELPERS['inventory'](path)['provenance']
assert sha(primary) == primary_sha
result = {'measured_at_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
          'scope': 'Separate diagnostics only; original primary samples and aggregates remain unchanged',
          'protocol': 'AB/BA/AB for each case; actual getters and unchanged timed measureBatch; runBench is byte-identical or has only separately verified call lowering outside the timer; 3 global warmups then calibration and minimum of ten batches; all builds finished before timing',
          'GOGC': '800', 'GOMAXPROCS': 'default', 'host_isolated': False,
          'source_comparison': 'generated-comparison.json', 'script_sha256': sha(__file__),
          'primary_campaign_sha256': primary_sha, 'cases': results, 'oracles_verified': 6 * len(cases),
          'original_generated_sources_and_binaries_unchanged': True}
(PROOF / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
print(json.dumps({key: {name: row[name] for name in ['case', 'source_suite', 'samples_us', 'medians_us', 'change_percent', 'increase_over_5_percent_reproduced']}
                  for key, row in results.items()}, indent=2))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Freeze the official 37-case Go/C baseline before changing hot-path codegen."""

ROOT = Path('/Users/0x1/Documents/htdocs/altbak.pub')

OLD = ROOT / 'var/benchmark/go-hotpaths-20261126'

sha = lambda p: hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
write = lambda p, x: Path(p).write_text(json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + '\n')
if (WORK / 'compiler-before/manifest.json').exists():
    raise ValueError('Refusing to overwrite the frozen compiler baseline')
history_path = ROOT / 'docs/benchmark-results/2026-11-26-go-hotpaths.json'
reference_path = ROOT / 'docs/benchmark-results/2026-11-26-c-library.json'
history = json.loads(history_path.read_text())

for name, digest in history['compiler']['measured_snapshot']['files_sha256'].items():
    assert sha(name) == digest, ('Compiler differs from measured previous executable', name)
manifest = {
    'head': subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(COMPILER), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip(),
    'status': subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(COMPILER), 'status', '--porcelain'], text=True),
    'sources': {}, 'files': {},
    'previous_measured_compiler_matches': True,
    'previous_measured_head': history['compiler']['measured_snapshot']['head'],
    'note': 'Measured baseline preserving the current tracked and untracked source state; all 204 measured compiler source and executable hashes match the previous record projection campaign. The recorded status determines whether this snapshot is clean or dirty.',
}
manifest['baseline_kind'] = 'dirty measured snapshot' if manifest['status'] else 'clean measured snapshot'
tracked = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(COMPILER), 'ls-files', '--cached', '--others', '--exclude-standard'], text=True).splitlines()
manifest['source_inventory'] = sorted(set(tracked))
manifest['missing_source_files'] = [name for name in sorted(set(tracked)) if not (COMPILER / name).is_file()]
extra = ['bin/gopurs', 'bin/gopurs-native', 'bin/gopurs.js',
         'src/Gopurs/Runtime/Source.go', 'src/Gopurs/Runtime/Source.js', 'src/Gopurs/Runtime/Source.rs']
for group, names in [('sources', tracked), ('files', extra)]:
    for name in names:
        source = COMPILER / name
        if not source.is_file():
            continue
        target = WORK / 'compiler-before' / group / name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(source, target)
        manifest[group][name] = {'path': str(target), 'sha256': sha(target)}
        assert sha(source) == sha(target)
mp = WORK / 'compiler-before/manifest.json'
write(mp, manifest)
shutil.copy2(ROOT / 'README.md', WORK / 'README.before.md')
frozen = json.loads((OLD / 'proofs/campaign-scripts/freeze.json').read_text())
for name, digest in frozen['source_sha256'].items():
    assert sha(ROOT / name) == digest, ('Previously protected source changed', name)
protected = [path for folder in ('src', 'srx', 'bin/benchmark', 'bin/native')
             for path in (ROOT / folder).rglob('*') if path.is_file() and '__pycache__' not in path.parts]
protected += [ROOT / 'tmp/bench_native.c', ROOT / 'tmp/imperative_reference_contract.md', history_path, reference_path]
protected += [path for path in (ROOT / 'tmp/c-library').iterdir() if path.is_file()]
frozen['source_sha256'].update({str(path.relative_to(ROOT)): sha(path) for path in protected})
ports = [(ROOT / json.loads(match[1])).resolve() for match in
         re.finditer(r'(?m)^\s*path:\s*("(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*")\s*$', (ROOT / 'run/bak/go/spago.go.yaml').read_text())]
frozen['library_sources_sha256'] = {
    str(path): sha(path) for port in ports for path in (port / 'src').rglob('*') if path.is_file()}
frozen['library_git_heads'] = {str(port): subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(port), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip()
                               for port in ports}
frozen['compiler_head'] = manifest['head']
frozen['compiler_baseline_manifest'] = str(mp)
frozen['compiler_baseline_manifest_sha256'] = sha(mp)
frozen['historical_archive'] = {'path': str(history_path.relative_to(ROOT)), 'sha256': sha(history_path)}
frozen['reference37_archive'] = {'path': str(reference_path.relative_to(ROOT)), 'sha256': sha(reference_path)}
campaign = history['campaign']
frozen['historical_go_core_times_us'] = campaign['primary_times_us']['after']
frozen['historical_go_all_times_us'] = {name: row['medians_us']['after'] for name, row in campaign['all_campaign']['all_tests'].items()}
frozen['historical_go37_times_us'] = campaign['matched37_times_us']['after']
frozen['c37_times_us'] = {name: entry['time_us'] for name, entry in reference['publication']['references']['columns']['c'].items() if name in frozen['historical_go37_times_us']}
frozen['c37_times_us'].update(reference['medians_us'])
assert set(frozen['c37_times_us']) == set(frozen['historical_go37_times_us']) and len(frozen['c37_times_us']) == 37
frozen['historical_aggregates'] = campaign['core14_aggregates']['after']
frozen['historical37_aggregates'] = {key: campaign['aggregates']['after'][source] for key, source in [('/', 'total'), ('μ', 'arithmetic'), ('Q₂', 'median'), ('G', 'geometric')]}
frozen['compiler_baseline_kind'] = manifest['baseline_kind']
frozen['documentary_baseline_sha256'] = {'README.md': sha(ROOT / 'README.md')}
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark'))
C = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/compare-core.py'))
J = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/js-ratios.py'))
for kind in ('core', 'all'):
    source = OLD / ('after-' + kind)
    destination = WORK / ('before-' + kind)
    shutil.copytree(source, destination)
    assert sha(source / 'benchmark') == sha(destination / 'benchmark')
    frozen['go_before_' + kind + '_directory'] = str(destination)
    frozen['go_before_' + kind + '_directory_binary_sha256'] = sha(destination / 'benchmark')
    frozen['go_before_' + kind + '_directory_manifest_sha256'] = sha(destination / 'manifest.json')
frozen['go_before_core'] = C['inspect_go'](WORK / 'before-core')
frozen['go_before_all'] = {'directory': str(WORK / 'before-all'), 'manifest': J['inspect'](WORK / 'before-all'),
                         'manifest_sha256': sha(WORK / 'before-all/manifest.json')}
for name in ('references.json', 'collect-all.py', 'inputs.json'):
    shutil.copy2(OLD / 'proofs/campaign-scripts' / name, SCRIPTS / name)
frozen['reference_files_sha256'] = {str(SCRIPTS / name): sha(SCRIPTS / name) for name in ('references.json', 'collect-all.py')}
write(SCRIPTS / 'freeze.json', frozen)
for group in ('sources', 'files'):
    for name, entry in manifest[group].items():
        assert sha(COMPILER / name) == entry['sha256'], ('Compiler changed while freezing', name)
assert manifest['status'] == subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(COMPILER), 'status', '--porcelain'], text=True)
print(json.dumps({'head': manifest['head'], 'compiler_sources': len(manifest['sources']), 'protected_sources': len(frozen['source_sha256']),
                  'before_core_sha256': frozen['go_before_core_directory_binary_sha256'],
                  'before_all_sha256': frozen['go_before_all_directory_binary_sha256'],
                  'cases': 37, 'historical_aggregates': frozen['historical37_aggregates']}, indent=2))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pair frozen Go App/AppAll builds against all 37 unchanged archived C medians."""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import runpy
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
ROOT = Path('/Users/0x1/Documents/htdocs/altbak.pub')
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark'))
C = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/compare-core.py'))
J = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/js-ratios.py'))


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def write(path, value):
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + '\n')


def metrics(times, reference):
    if set(times) != set(reference) or len(times) not in (14, 37):
        raise ValueError('Identical Go/C case populations of 14 or 37 required')
    ratios = [times[name] / reference[name] for name in times]
    if any(not math.isfinite(x) or x <= 0 for x in ratios):
        raise ValueError('Invalid ratio')
    return {'total': sum(times.values()) / sum(reference.values()),
            'arithmetic': statistics.mean(ratios), 'median': statistics.median(ratios),
            'geometric': math.exp(statistics.mean(math.log(x) for x in ratios))}


def verify_freeze(frozen):
    if 'benchmark_baseline_manifest' in frozen:
        benchmark_manifest=Path(frozen['benchmark_baseline_manifest'])
        assert sha(benchmark_manifest)==frozen['benchmark_baseline_manifest_sha256']
        baseline_benchmark=json.loads(benchmark_manifest.read_text())
        for name,entry in baseline_benchmark['preserved_existing_files'].items():
            assert sha(entry['snapshot'])==entry['sha256'], ('Changed benchmark snapshot',name)
            if name!='README.md':
                assert sha(ROOT/name)==entry['sha256'], ('Changed prior publication',name)
    baseline_path = Path(frozen['compiler_baseline_manifest'])
    if sha(baseline_path) != frozen['compiler_baseline_manifest_sha256']:
        raise ValueError('Compiler baseline manifest changed')
    baseline = json.loads(baseline_path.read_text())
    for group in ['files', 'sources']:
        C['verify_hashes']({entry['path']: entry['sha256'] for entry in baseline[group].values()})
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['source_sha256'], ROOT)
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['library_sources_sha256'])
    C['verify_hashes'](frozen['reference_files_sha256'])
    for build in [frozen['go_before_core'], frozen['c_build']]:
        C['verify_hashes']({build['manifest_path']: build['manifest_sha256']})
        C['verify_hashes'](build['payload_sha256'])
    old_all = frozen['go_before_all']
    path = Path(old_all['directory'])
    C['verify_hashes']({str(path / 'manifest.json'): old_all['manifest_sha256'],
                       str(path / 'benchmark'): old_all['manifest']['binary_sha256']})


def compiler_snapshot():
    root = ROOT.parent / 'gopurs/gopurs'
    paths = [root / 'bin/gopurs-native', root / 'bin/gopurs.js', root / 'bin/gopurs']
    paths += [path for folder in ['src', 'runtime'] for path in sorted((root / folder).rglob('*'))
              if path.is_file() and path.suffix in {'.purs', '.go', '.js', '.rs'}]
    return {'root': str(root),
            'head': subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(root), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip(),
            'files_sha256': {str(path): sha(path) for path in paths}}


def plan_entry(key, build):
    return {'key': key, 'mode': 'pure', 'command': build['command'],
            'artifact': build['cwd'], 'cwd': build['cwd'],
            'manifest': build['manifest_path'], 'manifest_sha256': build['manifest_sha256'],
            'payload_sha256': build['payload_sha256'],
            'executable_sha256': build['manifest']['binary_sha256']}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--freeze', type=Path, default=Path(__file__).with_name('freeze.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--after-core', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--after-all', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--execute', action='store_true', help='run only after all builds and tests have finished')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    frozen = json.loads(args.freeze.read_text())
    verify_freeze(frozen)
    before_core = C['inspect_go'](Path(frozen['go_before_core']['cwd']))
    after_core = C['inspect_go'](args.after_core.resolve())
    before_all = J['inspect'](Path(frozen['go_before_all']['directory']))
    after_all = J['inspect'](args.after_all.resolve())
    for label, before, after in [('core', before_core['manifest'], after_core['manifest']),
                                 ('all', before_all, after_all)]:
        for field in ['profile', 'toolchain']:
            if before[field] != after[field]:
                raise ValueError(f'{label} build {field} differs')
        for name in before['inputs']:
            if name.startswith(('src/', 'srx/')) and before['inputs'][name] != after['inputs'].get(name):
                raise ValueError(f'{label} benchmark input differs: {name}')
    if before_core['command'] == after_core['command'] or Path(frozen['go_before_all']['directory']) == args.after_all.resolve():
        raise ValueError('Distinct before/after builds are required')
    plan = [plan_entry('before', before_core), plan_entry('after', after_core)]
    if not args.execute:
        print(json.dumps({'validated': True, 'core_plan': plan,
                          'all_pair': [frozen['go_before_all']['directory'], str(args.after_all.resolve())],
                          'C_reference_remeasured': False, 'processes': 12}, indent=2))
        return
    args.output = args.output.resolve()
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    write(args.output / 'freeze.json', frozen)
    write(args.output / 'core-plan.json', plan)
    env = dict(os.environ, GOGC='800')
    for key in ['GOMAXPROCS', 'PPROF']:
        env.pop(key, None)
    compiler = compiler_snapshot()
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    load_start = list(os.getloadavg())
    commands = [
        [sys.executable, '-B', str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/measure.py'), '--plan',
         str(args.output / 'core-plan.json'), '--output', str(args.output / 'core')],
        [sys.executable, '-B', str(Path(__file__).with_name('collect-all.py')), '--before',
         frozen['go_before_all']['directory'], '--after', str(args.after_all.resolve()),
         '--output', str(args.output / 'all')],
    ]
    for command in commands:
        verify_freeze(frozen)
        C['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
        subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, env=env, check=True)
        verify_freeze(frozen)
        C['verify_hashes'](compiler['files_sha256'])
    core = json.loads((args.output / 'core/results.json').read_text())
    all_cases = json.loads((args.output / 'all/results.json').read_text())
    labels = C['ROWS']
    core_times = {variant: dict(zip(labels, data['times_us'])) for variant, data in core.items()}
    core_aggregates = {variant: metrics(times, frozen['c_times_us']) for variant, times in core_times.items()}
    core_historical = metrics(frozen['historical_go_core_times_us'], frozen['c_times_us'])
    for key, value in core_historical.items():
        if not math.isclose(value, frozen['historical_aggregates'][key], rel_tol=1e-12):
            raise ValueError('Historical metrics do not reproduce the official archive')
    # Preserve the publication's primary App medians for core14, and use AppAll
    # for library23 only. Both sides of every aggregate now contain all 37 cases.
    matched37 = {
        variant: {name: core_times[variant][name] if name in core_times[variant]
                  else row['medians_us'][variant]
                  for name, row in all_cases['all_tests'].items()}
        for variant in ('before', 'after')}
    aggregates = {variant: metrics(times, frozen['c37_times_us']) for variant, times in matched37.items()}
    historical = metrics(frozen['historical_go37_times_us'], frozen['c37_times_us'])
    for key, prior_key in [('total', '/'), ('arithmetic', 'μ'), ('median', 'Q₂'), ('geometric', 'G')]:
        if not math.isclose(historical[key], frozen['historical37_aggregates'][prior_key], rel_tol=1e-12):
            raise ValueError('Historical 37-case metrics do not reproduce the official README')
    rows = []
    for name in matched37['after']:
        before, after = matched37['before'][name], matched37['after'][name]
        if name in labels:
            index = labels.index(name)
            samples = {variant: [sample['times_us'][index] for sample in core[variant]['process_runs']]
                       for variant in ['before', 'after']}
        else:
            samples = all_cases['all_tests'][name]['samples_us']
        rows.append({'case': name, 'times_us': {'before': before, 'after': after, 'c': frozen['c37_times_us'][name]},
                     'go_over_c': {variant: times[name] / frozen['c37_times_us'][name] for variant, times in matched37.items()},
                     'samples_us': samples, 'speedup': before / after, 'change_percent': 100 * (after / before - 1),
                     'before_over_historical': before / frozen['historical_go37_times_us'][name]})
    all_regressions = sorted([{'case': name, 'change_percent': case['change_percent'],
                              'medians_us': case['medians_us'], 'samples_us': case['samples_us']}
                             for name, case in all_cases['all_tests'].items() if case['change_percent'] > 5],
                            key=lambda row: -row['change_percent'])
    raw_core = {path.name: path.read_text() for suffix in ['stdout', 'stderr']
                for path in sorted((args.output / 'core').glob('*.' + suffix))}
    report = {'started_at_utc': started, 'completed_at_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
              'host': platform.platform(), 'machine': platform.machine(), 'host_isolated': False,
              'load_average_start': load_start, 'load_average_end': list(os.getloadavg()),
              'protocol': {'paired_order': 'AB/BA/AB', 'processes_per_build': 3,
                           'primary': '14 App core medians plus 23 AppAll library medians; all four Go/C aggregates use 37 matched cases',
                           'GOGC': '800', 'GOMAXPROCS': 'default', 'pgo': False,
                           'C_reference_remeasured': False, 'JS_reference_remeasured': False,
                           'aggregation': 'median of three process minima for each case'},
              'commands': commands, 'wrapper_sha256': sha(Path(__file__)),
              'frozen_reference': frozen, 'compiler_snapshot': compiler, 'aggregates': aggregates, 'historical_aggregates': historical,
              'primary_times_us': core_times, 'primary_total_ms': {k: sum(v.values())/1000 for k,v in core_times.items()},
              'matched37_times_us': matched37, 'matched37_total_ms': {k: sum(v.values())/1000 for k,v in matched37.items()},
              'core14_aggregates': core_aggregates, 'historical_core14_aggregates': core_historical,
              'c_total_ms': sum(frozen['c37_times_us'].values())/1000,
              'rows_by_go_c_descending': sorted(rows, key=lambda r: -r['go_over_c']['after']),
              'all_case_regressions_over_5_percent': all_regressions,
              'validation': {'processes': 12, 'core_oracles': 84, 'all_oracles': 222,
                             'total_oracles': 306, 'source_and_binary_guards': True},
              'core_manifest': json.loads((args.output / 'core/manifest.json').read_text()),
              'core_campaign': core, 'raw_core_outputs': raw_core, 'all_campaign': all_cases}
    write(args.output / 'results.json', report)
    print(json.dumps({'aggregates': aggregates, 'historical': historical,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only independent consistency checks for the archived hot-path campaign."""
import base64, hashlib, json, runpy, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ROOT = WORK.parents[2]
path = ROOT / 'docs/benchmark-results/2026-11-26-go-runtime-calls.json'
raw = path.read_bytes()
archive = json.loads(raw)
sha = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
count = 0


def visit(value):
    global count
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if isinstance(value.get('text'), str) and 'sha256' in value:
            assert sha(value['text'].encode()) == value['sha256']
            count += 1
        if isinstance(value.get('base64'), str) and 'sha256' in value:
            assert sha(base64.b64decode(value['base64'])) == value['sha256']
        for child in value.values():
            visit(child)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for child in value:
            visit(child)


visit(archive)
helper = runpy.run_path(str(Path(__file__).with_name('archive.py')))
checks = helper['check_campaign'](archive['campaign'])
assert checks == archive['validation']['archive_checks']
for name,check in [('runtime_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_inputs'](archive['campaign'])),('alias_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_alias_inputs'](archive['campaign'])),('compact_alias_input_proofs',lambda:helper['check_alias_inputs'](archive['campaign'],compact=True))]:
    if archive['validation'][name].get('performed') is not False:
        assert check()==archive['validation'][name]
    else:
        assert archive['validation'][name]['total_oracles']==0
assert helper['check_diagnostics'](archive['campaign']) == archive['validation']['diagnostic_checks']
assert archive['validation']['final_summary'] == json.loads((WORK / 'validation-summary.json').read_text())
assert archive['report']['text'] == (ROOT / archive['report']['path']).read_text()
for name, evidence in archive['validation']['logs'].items():
    assert sha((WORK / name).read_bytes()) == evidence['sha256'], name
for name, evidence in archive['proofs']['runtime_inputs_and_collectors'].items():
    assert sha((WORK / 'proofs' / name).read_bytes()) == evidence['sha256'], name
for name, evidence in archive['proofs']['supporting_files'].items():
    assert sha((WORK / name).read_bytes()) == evidence['sha256'], name
assert not (ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/ratio-measurements.json').exists()
print(json.dumps({'path': str(path), 'bytes': len(raw), 'sha256': sha(raw),
                  'embedded_text_hashes_verified': count, 'campaign': checks,
                  'runtime_oracles': archive['validation']['runtime_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'alias_oracles': archive['validation']['alias_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'compact_alias_oracles': archive['validation']['compact_alias_input_proofs']['total_oracles'],
                  'removed_catalogue_remains_absent': True}, indent=2))

import Effect (Effect)

foreign import identity :: forall a. a -> Effect a
foreign import snapshot :: Effect String
foreign import reset :: Effect Unit

literalInt :: Unit -> Effect Int
literalInt _ = do
  value <- identity 41
  pure (value + 1)

literalText :: Unit -> Effect String
literalText _ = do
  value <- identity "retained"
  pure (value <> "!")

changing :: Ref.Ref Int -> Effect Int
changing ref = do
  input <- Ref.read ref
  value <- identity input
  pure value

changingWithContinuation :: Ref.Ref Int -> Effect Int
changingWithContinuation ref = do
  input <- Ref.read ref
  value <- identity input
  pure (value + 1)

nested :: Int -> Effect Int
nested input = do
  left <- identity input
  right <- identity (left + 1)
  pure (left + right)

main :: Effect Unit

  logShow =<< literalInt unit
  logShow =<< literalInt unit
  log =<< literalText unit
  ref <- Ref.new 7
  logShow =<< changing ref
  logShow =<< changingWithContinuation ref
  Ref.write 11 ref
  logShow =<< changing ref
  logShow =<< changingWithContinuation ref
  logShow =<< nested 10
  array <- identity [ 2, 4 ]
  logShow array
  record <- identity { count: 17 }
  logShow record.count
  callback <- identity (\value -> value + 3)
  logShow (callback 4)
  saved <- identity (identity 23)
  logShow =<< saved
  logShow =<< saved
  log =<< snapshot

module Main where

-- @dependencies: prelude effect console refs

import Prelude
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (log, logShow)
import Effect.Ref as Ref

foreign import identity :: forall a. a -> Effect a
foreign import snapshot :: Effect String
foreign import reset :: Effect Unit

literalInt :: Unit -> Effect Int
literalInt _ = do
  value <- identity 41
  pure (value + 1)

literalText :: Unit -> Effect String
literalText _ = do
  value <- identity "retained"
  pure (value <> "!")

changing :: Ref.Ref Int -> Effect Int
changing ref = do
  input <- Ref.read ref
  value <- identity input
  pure value

changingWithContinuation :: Ref.Ref Int -> Effect Int
changingWithContinuation ref = do
  input <- Ref.read ref
  value <- identity input
  pure (value + 1)

nested :: Int -> Effect Int
nested input = do
  left <- identity input
  right <- identity (left + 1)
  pure (left + right)

main :: Effect Unit
main = do
  reset
  logShow =<< literalInt unit
  logShow =<< literalInt unit
  log =<< literalText unit
  ref <- Ref.new 7
  logShow =<< changing ref
  logShow =<< changingWithContinuation ref
  Ref.write 11 ref
  logShow =<< changing ref
  logShow =<< changingWithContinuation ref
  logShow =<< nested 10
  array <- identity [ 2, 4 ]
  logShow array
  record <- identity { count: 17 }
  logShow record.count
  callback <- identity (\value -> value + 3)
  logShow (callback 4)
  saved <- identity (identity 23)
  logShow =<< saved
  logShow =<< saved
  log =<< snapshot

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. # 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

campaign/core/README.before.md.text:
# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio.
